scopeAndAssumptions.label: Process
scopeAndAssumptions.text: aseptic filling of a sterile, small-volume injectable into glass vials on a RABS (restricted access barrier system) line, with Grade A filling inside a Grade B background. The scope runs from component preparation through batch disposition.

scopeAndAssumptions.label: Environmental monitoring (EM) program
scopeAndAssumptions.text: viable air sampling (active and settle plates), surface contact plates, personnel monitoring (gloves and gowns), and continuous non-viable particle counting.

scopeAndAssumptions.label: AI component
scopeAndAssumptions.text: Sterile Sense AI is assumed to review EM results from the lab system, flag results above alert and action limits, spot adverse trends, and suggest what QA should look at. QA microbiology makes every decision. This describes a hypothetical use for analysis, not a statement of current product capability.

scopeAndAssumptions.label: Out of scope
scopeAndAssumptions.text: drug substance manufacturing, sterile filtration of bulk product, terminal inspection beyond closure checks, and lab methods for identifying organisms.

scopeAndAssumptions.label: Framework
scopeAndAssumptions.text: structure follows the general approach of ICH Q9(R1), Quality Risk Management. Relevant guidance for aseptic processing includes EU GMP Annex 1 and FDA's guidance on sterile drug products produced by aseptic processing.

processSteps.name: Prepare and sterilize components and equipment (vials, stoppers, product-contact parts)
Gown up and enter the cleanroom
Set up the line and perform aseptic interventions
Review EM data with AI assistance (Sterile Sense AI plus QA microbiology)

failureModes.stepName: Prepare and sterilize components and equipment (vials, stoppers, product-contact parts)
failureModes.failureMode: Components or parts not fully sterilized or depyrogenated
failureModes.effect: Non-sterile or pyrogenic surfaces touch the product
failureModes.cause: Wrong load pattern; cycle or depyrogenation tunnel fault
failureModes.detectionControls: Cycle record review; biological and endotoxin indicators

failureModes.stepName: Gown up and enter the cleanroom
failureModes.failureMode: Gowning breach (exposed skin, torn glove, poor donning)
failureModes.effect: Operator sheds particles and microbes into the critical zone
failureModes.detectionControls: Glove and gown sampling at exit

failureModes.stepName: Set up the line and perform aseptic interventions
failureModes.failureMode: Poor aseptic technique during an intervention (e.g., blocking airflow over open vials)
failureModes.effect: Direct contamination risk to open product
failureModes.preventionControls: Defined intervention list; interventions included in media fills

recommendedActions.action: Trend sterilization and depyrogenation cycle data; verify load patterns at each run
Requalify gowning on a regular schedule; sample gloves and gowns at every exit from the critical area
Reduce interventions through equipment design; record and review interventions on video; cover every intervention type in media fills
Test glove integrity before each batch; set glove change frequency from failure history
Interlock filling with airflow and pressure alarms so filling stops when conditions are lost
Add automatic reject for vials with missing or misplaced stoppers
Use an electronic EM schedule with barcode-scanned sample locations and missed-sample alerts
Barcode-label plates; track incubation in the lab system
Evaluate the model on historical EM data enriched with known excursions and trends against predefined acceptance criteria; keep mandatory QA review of all EM data
Feed counts to the AI directly from the lab system; require second-person verification for any manual edit
Have reviewers assess the raw EM data before the AI's summary is shown ("blind-first" review); audit a sample of reviews
Bring EM location, limit, and equipment changes under change control so they trigger model re-evaluation; monitor AI–human agreement rates
Log model version, inputs, outputs, reviewer ID, timestamps, and overrides in a tamper-evident audit trail
Have the system block disposition until all EM results are final and reviewed; require a QA second signature for any override

topRisksSummary.label: QA trusting the AI's "no issues" too much (RPN 270)
topRisksSummary.text: EM data is high-volume and mostly clean, which is exactly when people stop looking. If reviewers rely on the AI, the main human control over contamination signals is gone.

topRisksSummary.label: Poor technique during aseptic interventions (RPN 240)
topRisksSummary.text: Every time an operator reaches into the critical zone, open product is at risk. The best fix is fewer interventions, not just more watching.

topRisksSummary.label: Wrong counts going into the AI (RPN 192)
topRisksSummary.text: The AI can only be as good as its data. Manual transcription of plate counts quietly corrupts every trend downstream.

topRisksSummary.label: Gowning breaches (RPN 180)
topRisksSummary.text: People are the largest contamination source in aseptic areas, and a small gown or glove failure can go unnoticed during a shift.

topRisksSummary.label: Missed or misplaced EM samples (RPN 160)
topRisksSummary.text: If a sample isn't taken where and when it should be, contamination can happen without leaving any evidence for the AI or QA to review.
